subject: Performance SLOs and context window for FinCo integration — recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ella Thompson <ella@finco.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-08T15:10:00Z
Subject: Performance SLOs and context window for FinCo integration — recap & next steps

Hi Ella,

Thanks again for the call today — good discussion and really helpful context about the compliance and latency needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Summary of FinCo requirements (from call):
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile time-to-first-token (TTFT) <= 600ms for interactive flows; steady-state token gen latency target ~<= 50ms/token for streaming outputs.
- Throughput / concurrency: support up to 25 QPS at peak, with ~40 concurrent sessions (typical concurrency per user ~1-2, spikes to 6-8).
- Context window: need support for up to 32k tokens (input + output). Typical example is ~20k input tokens (long doc + retrieval) + ~2k output tokens.
- Streaming: required for user-facing flows (partial output must arrive as generated).
- Availability: production SLA expected; will discuss Dedicated/reserved capacity if benchmarks look good.

Potential performance impact / considerations we flagged:
- Large context windows (16k–32k) increase attention compute (quadratic effects), KV cache size, and memory working set — this will raise per-request latency compared to shorter contexts.
- Streaming mitigates perceived latency (TTFT), but total tail latency for long-context generation can still be affected by model choice and hardware.
- To meet both context and latency targets we may recommend: a 32k-capable model with quantization + optimized kernels, plus prefix/KV caching and selective retrieval windowing. In some cases a 16k variant with chunked retrieval + re-attend strategy provides better latency for interactive flows, with fallback to full 32k for background/async jobs.

Next steps (proposed):
1) SE perf validation: David to run targeted perf runs against a Dedicated A100 cluster using FinCo sample payloads (we'll mirror the 20k token inputs + 2k outputs). Deliverables: detailed latency percentiles, token/sec, and memory footprint.
2) Benchmark share: we'll push a perf run and sample artifacts (pdf/csv) to you and the HubSpot deal.
3) Pricing/commit guidance: Rishi will provide a rough capacity-based pricing estimate after the perf run.
4) Schedule: propose perf run week of Jul 13; follow-up demo + results on Jul 15.

I've attached a short perf-run summary template and included sample payloads in the shared artifact. Please confirm the perf window and whether you'd like us to include additional input shapes (e.g., many small docs vs one massive doc).

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

- When you say 95th TTFT <= 600ms, is that measured on the first token arriving at the client over streaming, or the first token reached by the model runtime? We care about client experience (first byte to browser).

Also could you include a rough ballpark for monthly committed capacity pricing for a Dedicated pool that handles these numbers (so we can flag budget with procurement)? No need for exact contract terms yet — just high level.

Ella — good questions. Short answers: 
- TTFT measurement: we'll report both runtime-first-token (model runtime) and end-to-client (including network/serialization) metrics. For the SLO we'll aim to ensure end-to-client 95th <= 600ms on our Dedicated deployment under the defined load (we'll instrument from a browser agent in the perf tests).
- Pricing: Rishi will send a back-of-envelope committed capacity estimate once we have the perf results. As a ballpark for planning, Dedicated reserved capacity for this profile (32k-capable instances, sustained peak ~25 QPS, headroom for spikes) typically maps to mid-six-figure ARR territory — we'll give a more precise number after the run.

David (SE) — I captured a few technical notes in-line below; can you validate feasibility and the test plan?

> From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
> Date: 2026-07-09T13:30:00Z
> Subject: SE notes (performance considerations)
>
> Quick notes on context window impact:
> - Self-attention compute grows roughly O(n^2) with sequence length; moving from 16k -> 32k has ~4x attention compute in the worst case.
> - For streaming TTFT we can hide some latency by emitting initial tokens early (prefix-only attention on the prompt), but long cross-attention/re-encoding steps for very large contexts still add to tail.
> - Mitigations: sparse/longformer-style attention, sliding-window + chunked retrieval + re-ranking, and prefix caching. Also model distillation to a 16k variant for interactive flows is a practical compromise.
> - Hardware: A100 class GPUs with optimized kernels (cuBLAS/FlashAttention variants) are preferred; we'll evaluate quantized kernels if memory pressure is high.
>
> Proposed test plan:
> 1) Reproduce FinCo sample inputs (20k token doc + typical retrieval noise).
> 2) Run steady-state throughput test at 25 QPS and spike tests to 40 QPS.
> 3) Measure: TTFT (runtime + end-to-client), p50/p90/p95 token latencies, tokens/sec, GPU memory, and KV cache sizes.
> 4) Evaluate 16k vs 32k model variants and streaming behavior.
>
> I'll run the first perf batch on a Dedicated A100 pool and upload the results to the dashboard.
>
> —David
> Senior Solutions Engineer

I'll schedule the perf run for the week of Jul 13 and share the results + a short slide pack.

Marissa
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T11:05:00Z
Subject: RE: SE notes / perf validation plan for FinCo

Marissa / Rishi — quick technical addendum to confirm what we'll measure and the likely outcomes based on prior runs:

1) Context window impact and numbers (estimate):
- 8k -> 16k: ~3.5x increase in attention time for long, dense inputs.
- 16k -> 32k: additional ~3.8x on top of that (so ~13x versus 8k in worst case for naive dense attention). These are rough upper bounds; optimized kernels and sparsity reduce this in practice.

2) Streaming strategy:
- For interactive flows, we should prioritize time-to-first-token via early emission (emit tokens as soon as the decoder has something stable to send). That gets TTFT down even with large contexts.
- For heavy retrieval contexts, plan to maintain a sliding window (e.g., last 8–12k tokens) for immediate response and perform a secondary pass for full 32k context when needed (async). That pattern keeps interactive latency low while preserving full-context accuracy for non-interactive use-cases.

3) Feasibility callouts:
- If FinCo insists on strict 95th end-to-client <= 600ms for full 32k synchronous responses at peak QPS, that will be very challenging on current gen hardware without materially higher compute (more GPUs per request) or algorithmic sparsity.
- Alternate: aim for 95th <= 600ms for the interactive streaming-first-token case and 95th <= 2.5–4s for full synchronous 32k responses (documented as an expected behavior).

4) Test resources requested:
- Dedicated A100 pool (4–8 cards) for two full runs (16k and 32k).
- Sample payloads (provided by FinCo).

I'll kick off the 16k run first and report numbers; we'll use that to inform Rishi's pricing sketch.

—David
